paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus faces the devil's temptations with the Word of God. He is hungry after forty days, and the devil comes at Him three different ways. Every time, Jesus answers with the words of Scripture (Luke 4:4, 8, 12), and the Bible says He was “full of the Holy Spirit” the whole way (Luke 4:1). He doesn't argue and He doesn't scramble, because He knows what God has said, and He stands on it.

Now look at round three, because this one is sneaky, and the devil quotes Scripture too: “For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully…’” (Luke 4:10). So knowing the words is not enough, friend. Jesus answers, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’” (Luke 4:12), so He knows what the whole Word says and what God meant by it. That's why I want you in the Word, baker, because Scripture read in pieces can be bent, and Scripture read whole holds steady.

And here's the part that should make you smile: the devil “left Him until an opportune time” (Luke 4:13), so the temptations weren't over for good, and yours won't be either. But Jesus showed you what to hold onto when they come back. Don't hold on to your own strength, because mine runs out around the time the timer goes off and the cookies start calling my name. Hold on to what God has said, and keep filling up on it, one passage at a time.
